applies_to: Dwyer Series MSX-Comms Magnesense differential pressure transmitters with BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU output.
summary: The MSX-Comms is a differential pressure transmitter for building air systems that can also calculate velocity or duct flow. Over BACnet MS/TP it reports the pressure in four units, velocity and flow, high and low alarm states, and exposes the process mode, K factor, duct area, alarm limits, damping and a zero calibration command.
notes: Device instance and name are 607XXX / "MSX 607XXX", where XXX is the address set on the DIP switches. Object instances (AI 1, AV 1 ...) are fixed.
Names follow the Object_Name defaults on the object pages; the summary table prints slightly different labels (for example "Pressure in w.c", "Flow Area sq ft").

Access is from the "Is (User) Writable" column. That column marks AV 5, AV 6 and BV 2 as not writable, but the text says AV 5/AV 6 are set over BACnet and BV 2 is written to zero the sensor, so they are shown as W. The alarm enables BV 5/BV 7 are printed not writable and kept as R.
AV 7, BV 1, BV 3 and BV 4 are not in the list. AV 9/AV 10 use the unit of the selected process mode.

source.title: Series MSX-Comms Magnesense Pressure Transmitter, Installation and Operating Instructions

integration.summary: Read the pressure AI in the unit you want, or the velocity/flow AV if the process mode is set to velocity or flow, and map the two alarm status BVs. Set MSV 1 Process Mode, the K factor and duct area once at commissioning.
setup: BACnet MS/TP or Modbus RTU on RS485; baud, parity and stop bits are detected automatically from bus traffic.
MAC address (0-127 for BACnet) is set on the DIP switches and also forms the device instance 607XXX.
DeviceCommunicationControl and ReinitializeDevice need the password given in the manual.
gotchas: Write BV 2 Zero only with atmospheric pressure on both ports.
Velocity and flow need the K factor (AV 5) and duct area (AV 6) set correctly.
